text_blocks.snippet: Chemotherapy is a cancer treatment that uses drugs to kill or slow the growth of cancer cells. It works by interfering with the cancer cells' ability to divide and multiply. Chemotherapy can be used to treat many types of cancer, often in combination with other treatments like surgery or radiation.
snippet_highlighted_words: a cancer treatment that uses drugs to kill or slow the growth of cancer cells

list.title: Targeting Rapidly Dividing Cells:
list.snippet: Chemotherapy drugs primarily target cells that divide and multiply quickly, which includes cancer cells.

list.title: Interfering with Cell Division:
list.snippet: These drugs can disrupt various processes involved in cell division, such as DNA replication or the formation of the structures that separate chromosomes.

list.title: Systemic Treatment:
list.snippet: Chemotherapy is often administered intravenously (through a vein) or orally (as pills), allowing it to travel throughout the body and target cancer cells wherever they may be.
